study.title: Antidepressant Monotherapy and Combination Therapy with Acupuncture in Depressed Patients: A Resting-State Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) Study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial; open-label with wait-list control group
study.randomization: Block randomization generated by MS Excel
study.blinding: Only the accessor was blinded throughout the whole study
study.population: Depression patients recruited from Queen Mary Hospital, The Mental Health Association of Hong Kong, Dance with Depression Association, Hong Kong Depression Disorder Support, and through community postings
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) aged between 18 and 65 years old, (2) right-handed, (3) met the criteria of depression in DSM-V, (4) regular intake of antidepressants at a fixed dose for at least 3 months before baseline and during the study period, (5) 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) score ≥ 8 and Patients Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) score ≥ 10 at baseline, and (6) provided a voluntary informed consent
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) Any history of psychosis or mania; (2) conditions that may make it difficult to conclusively determine that depressive symptoms are the result of depression and not some other condition (e.g., substance abuse or relevant medical conditions including epilepsy, and history of an abnormal EEG); (3) with a bleeding disorder or receiving anti-coagulants; (4) had infection or malignancy overlapping with the acupuncture sites; (5) had sensory neuropathies; (6) had serious uncontrolled medical conditions; (7) pregnant, breast-feeding, or childbearing potential but not using adequate contraception; (8) had received Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) in the past year; (9) received acupuncture 3 months before baseline; (10) change in antidepressant treatment within 4 weeks before baseline or during the study; (11) were current active suicidal or self-injurious potential that necessitated immediate treatment

arms.dropouts: 3 discontinued intervention (schedule unavailable to complete all treatment sessions), 1 lost to follow-up; additionally 3 excluded from analysis (did not receive intervention)

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: NIRSport (NIRx Medical Technologies LLC, Glen Head, NY, USA)
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Homer2 Matlab Source Code (homer2_src_v2_8_11022018-homer2_src_v2_8_11022018) based in Matlab (Mathworks.com)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: identify, remove or recalibrate channels with bad signals and long periods of motion artifacts using HomER2 built-in function (parameters set as tMotion = 3 s; tMAsk = 1.0)
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: band-pass filter applied to reduce physiological artifacts (0.01-0.2 Hz cut-off frequency)
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) via Pearson correlation coefficients between channels
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction; Bonferroni correction also mentioned for t-test familywise error control

additional_details.participant_position: supine, eyes closed, relaxed, 3-5 min rest before recording
additional_details.data_format_conversion: raw NIRS light intensity converted to optical density signal; filtered optical density converted to oxy-Hb, deoxy-Hb, and total-Hb
additional_details.fc_computation: hemodynamic changes between pre- and post-treatment converted into correlation coefficients indicating strength of functional connectivity among 18 channels
additional_details.channel_mapping: Channels 1-9 signify left hemisphere; Channels 10-18 signify right hemisphere; specifically channels F1, F3, AF3, AF7, FC3, FC5 (left DLPFC), AF8, F6 (right DLPFC) per 10-20 system

extraction_notes.note: The abstract states PHQ-9 between-group significance at 'Week 3 (p = 0.01)' but Table 3 shows the Week 3 row has p = 0.04 and the Week 2 row has p = 0.01. The results text states 'TG had significantly lower scores than CG at Week 3 (p = 0.01) and Week 4 (p = 0.04)' but Table 3 only shows through Week 3 with no Week 4 label. There appears to be a labeling discrepancy between abstract, results text, and Table 3 for PHQ-9 time points.
The HAMD-17 between-group p value is reported as p = 0.01 in the abstract but p = 0.015 in Table 4. Both values have been preserved as reported in their respective locations.

In Table 3, the 95% CI for the Treatment group PHQ-9 at Week 3 is listed as '(14.3 to 17.3)' which appears to be a copy/paste error from the Baseline row (TG Baseline 95%CI = 14.3 to 17.3). The mean value of 8.7 at Week 3 is inconsistent with a 95% CI of 14.3 to 17.3. This appears to be a typographical error in the paper.

The abstract states rsFC significance in 'F1, F3, AF3, AF7, FC3, FC5 (left DLPFC, 10–20 system), AF8, and F6 (right DLPFC)' but the results text describes significant channel pairs by channel number (1,3), (1,7), (2,17), (3,5), (3,8), (5,6), (5,7), (5,11). The mapping of channel numbers to 10-20 system labels is consistent with Figure 1 but is not explicitly tabulated.

The exact OHb correlation coefficient values for TG and CG for individual channel pairs are not separately reported per pair; the text gives a range 'r = 0.5 to 0.8 (TG); r = 0.05 to 0.4 (CG)' for all 8 significant OHb pairs collectively. Similarly for tHb. Individual pair-level r values are shown only in correlation matrix figures (Figs. 3, 4, 5) which cannot be precisely read from the PDF.

The correlation matrix maps (Figs. 3A, 4A, 5A) showing grand average functional connectivity values for CG and TG contain color-coded r values for all 18×18 channel combinations but individual values cannot be precisely extracted from the PDF figures. Precise per-pair r values are not available in tabular form.

The neuroimaging subsample for fNIRS analysis was described inconsistently: the abstract states '40 participants (20 control; 20 treatment) were randomized for studying functional connectivity'; the methods state 'data being available from 12 in the control group and 8 in the treatment group, a total of 20 participants' after exclusions. The final analyzed neuroimaging n = 20 (12 CG, 8 TG).

The paper states 'Bonferroni correction [*] was used to correct for the increased probability of an incorrect t-test result' but then reports results as 'p < 0.05, FDR corrected' and 'p < 0.01, FDR corrected'. It is unclear whether Bonferroni and FDR were both applied or whether the text contains an error. FDR is consistently mentioned in the figure legends and results, so FDR has been recorded as the primary correction method.
Sensory/interoceptive responses (deqi ratings, pain ratings) were not formally measured or quantitatively reported. De-qi was described only as 'triggered' and defined qualitatively.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported.

No coordinate space (MNI, Talairach, etc.) is applicable since this is an fNIRS study using the 10-20 electrode placement system rather than volumetric brain coordinates. No 3D brain coordinates are reported.

The clinical n for TG analyzed is inconsistent: Table 3 PHQ-9 analysis uses n=40 for Treatment group; Table 4 HAMD-17 analysis also uses n=40 for Treatment group; but the flow diagram shows 47 analyzed (50 assigned minus 3 excluded from analysis). The paper states 'n = 40' in Tables 3 and 4 which may represent the subset of TG who completed all PHQ-9 assessments.

The paper states two acupoint combinations (A and B) were assigned 'according to the patients' TCM syndrome' but does not report how many patients in each arm received each combination. TCM diagnosis was reported at baseline (Table 2) but not separately for subgroups receiving combination A vs B.

The HHb channel pair (12,18): both channels 12 and 18 are described as 'right hemisphere' per the convention that channels 10-18 = right hemisphere. This is consistent with the paper's channel labeling convention.

The paper states this is 'the first to apply the fNIRS in measuring the resting-state functional connectivity and investigate the mechanism of adjunctive acupuncture therapy with an antidepressant in depression patients.'
